lagna.Aries: Aries rising, ruled by Mars, gives a lean, athletic, energetic frame, often a prominent brow or a scar on the head, and a quick, direct gait. The native is courageous, self-starting, competitive and impatient with delay. Classical texts praise their initiative, leadership and frank speech. Challenges include temper, haste, accident-proneness around the head and a tendency to begin more than is finished. Mars as lagna lord is the key to the chart: its sign, house and dignity show where energy is spent and how vitality fares. Life themes revolve around independence, pioneering effort, physical courage and learning patience. Discipline and regular exercise turn raw drive into lasting achievement and protect health.
lagna.Taurus: Taurus rising, ruled by Venus, tends to give a sturdy, pleasant, well-proportioned body, a thick neck, attractive eyes and a calm, measured manner. The native is patient, loyal, practical and fond of comfort, food, music and beauty. Classical sources note determination, steady earning and a good voice. Challenges include stubbornness, possessiveness, sluggishness and weight or throat troubles. Venus as lagna lord shows how well pleasure, relationships and resources are managed; a strong Venus brings grace and material stability. Life themes center on building security, family values, wealth and craftsmanship. Flexibility and moderation in indulgence keep this steady nature from turning into rigidity.
lagna.Gemini: Gemini rising, ruled by Mercury, usually gives a slim, tall or lightly built body, long arms, expressive hands and a youthful look that lasts. The native is curious, witty, versatile and a quick learner who loves conversation, travel and information. Texts credit skill in speech, writing, trade and calculation. Challenges include restlessness, scattered focus, nervous tension and trouble with lungs, shoulders or nerves. Mercury as lagna lord governs intellect and adaptability; its condition shows whether cleverness matures into wisdom. Life themes involve communication, siblings, commerce and learning many skills. Depth, routine and a single main pursuit help convert abundant talent into recognised mastery.
lagna.Cancer: Cancer rising, ruled by the Moon, tends to give a rounded, softer body, a pale or gentle complexion, expressive face and a slightly fluctuating weight. The native is sensitive, protective, imaginative and strongly attached to home, mother and memory. Classical writers note kindness, a good memory and love of water or travel by it. Challenges include moodiness, over-worry, clinging and digestive or chest sensitivity. The Moon as lagna lord makes the whole life reflect emotional rhythms, so its phase, sign and house matter greatly. Life themes include nurturing, property, family roots and public connection. Emotional boundaries and a steady daily routine bring security and resilience.
lagna.Leo: Leo rising, ruled by the Sun, usually gives a strong, broad-shouldered frame, a dignified bearing, bold eyes and a commanding presence. The native is proud, generous, warm-hearted and has a natural wish to lead and be recognised. Classical texts mention courage, authority, love of forests and open places. Challenges include ego, a need for praise, stubbornness and heart, spine or blood-pressure vulnerability. The Sun as lagna lord shows the quality of confidence and the relationship with father figures and authority. Life themes involve leadership, creativity, government or position and learning humble service. Generosity without arrogance wins loyal followers and lasting respect.
lagna.Virgo: Virgo rising, ruled by Mercury, tends to give a neat, moderate, youthful body, a modest manner, clear features and careful movements. The native is analytical, helpful, discreet and attentive to detail, health and daily order. Classical sources credit skill in accounts, medicine, writing and craft. Challenges include over-criticism, anxiety, perfectionism and digestive or nervous disorders. Mercury as lagna lord, also lord of the tenth, joins mind and career, so its strength shapes success. Life themes revolve around service, work, health routines and refining skill. Self-acceptance and trust in the larger picture soften worry and let genuine competence shine.
lagna.Libra: Libra rising, ruled by Venus, generally gives a balanced, attractive body, a pleasing face, graceful movement and a diplomatic bearing. The native is fair-minded, sociable, artistic and seeks harmony in partnership and surroundings. Classical texts note a love of trade, justice, ornaments and refined company. Challenges include indecision, dependence on others' approval, avoidance of conflict and kidney or lower-back sensitivity. Venus as lagna lord, also ruling the eighth, ties relationships, resources and transformation together. Life themes include marriage, business partnerships, negotiation and aesthetics. Learning to decide and act without waiting for perfect balance makes this charm effective and respected.
lagna.Scorpio: Scorpio rising, ruled by Mars, tends to give a compact, strong body, penetrating eyes, magnetic presence and a guarded expression. The native is intense, resourceful, private and determined, with strong research and survival instincts. Classical writers note courage, secrecy and endurance through crises. Challenges include jealousy, resentment, controlling tendencies and troubles with the reproductive or excretory systems. Mars as lagna lord, with Ketu as co-ruler in some views, shows how drive is channeled. Life themes involve transformation, hidden matters, occult or investigative study, and regeneration after loss. Forgiveness and honest trust turn formidable willpower into healing and depth.
lagna.Sagittarius: Sagittarius rising, ruled by Jupiter, generally gives a tall, well-built frame, a broad forehead, open expression and an optimistic gait. The native is philosophical, honest, generous and drawn to learning, teachers, travel and faith. Classical texts credit wisdom, righteousness and skill in counsel or law. Challenges include overconfidence, bluntness, over-promising, weight gain and hip or liver issues. Jupiter as lagna lord, a natural benefic, tends to protect the life, and its placement shows the main field of grace. Life themes involve higher education, ethics, teaching, long journeys and finding purpose. Grounding ideals in practical follow-through brings lasting success and respect.
lagna.Capricorn: Capricorn rising, ruled by Saturn, often gives a lean, bony or wiry build, prominent joints, a serious look and a body that ages gracefully, often looking more mature young. The native is disciplined, patient, ambitious and responsible, preferring slow, solid progress. Classical sources note endurance, thrift and capacity for hard work. Challenges include pessimism, reserve, delayed rewards and knee, joint or skin troubles. Saturn as lagna lord shows how well the native handles duty and time; a strong Saturn gives status that builds with age. Life themes involve career, structure, responsibility and mastery. Warmth, rest and self-trust ease the burden of seriousness.
lagna.Aquarius: Aquarius rising, ruled by Saturn, generally gives a tall, well-framed body, an unusual or distinctive look, a calm eye and a detached manner. The native is independent, humane, inventive and friendly yet inwardly private. Classical texts mention scientific or social interests and steady, unconventional thinking. Challenges include aloofness, stubborn opinions, erratic emotional expression and circulation or ankle troubles. Saturn as lagna lord, with Rahu as modern co-ruler, links discipline with innovation. Life themes include friendships, networks, technology, reform and long-term gains through groups. Sharing feelings openly and committing to personal bonds balance the visionary mind.
lagna.Pisces: Pisces rising, ruled by Jupiter, tends to give a softer, medium frame, large, dreamy eyes, a gentle face and a tendency to weight changes. The native is compassionate, intuitive, imaginative and spiritually inclined, often absorbing the moods around them. Classical sources note charity, devotion and artistic or healing talent. Challenges include escapism, vagueness, poor boundaries, and sensitivity of feet, lymph and immunity. Jupiter as lagna lord promises protection, and its strength shows how faith and wisdom steady the life. Life themes include service, imagination, solitude, foreign lands and spiritual seeking. Practical routines and clear limits help dreams take form and conserve energy.

moon_sign.Aries: Moon in Aries gives an emotionally quick, spirited and direct mind. Feelings arise fast, are expressed openly and pass just as quickly. The native needs independence, activity and challenges to feel alive, and becomes restless or irritable when held back. Courage and initiative come naturally, yet patience with sensitivity in others must be learned. Nourishment comes from physical movement, competitive goals, honest talk and a sense of being first or free. Mars as sign lord links emotional health to vigor and sleep. Rest, cooling foods and calm routines help the heat of emotion settle.
moon_sign.Taurus: Moon in Taurus is exalted, bringing a stable, soothing and sensual emotional nature. The mind seeks steadiness, comfort and beauty, and gains peace from good food, music, nature and a secure home. Loyalty and patience are strong, as are attachment to people and possessions. Change unsettles this Moon, and it can become stubborn or hold on too long. Venus as sign lord adds affection and artistic taste. Nourishment comes from regular routine, touch, financial security and pleasant surroundings. Gentle movement and openness to change prevent complacency.
moon_sign.Gemini: Moon in Gemini gives a curious, talkative and quickly shifting mind. Emotions are processed through thinking, speaking and writing, and the native feels better when able to share ideas. Variety, company, reading and short trips nourish the spirit, while monotony causes restlessness. The mind may be anxious or scattered under stress, with many thoughts at once. Mercury as sign lord shows a youthful, adaptable emotional style. Stability comes from journaling, rest for the nerves, trusted friends and giving attention to one thing at a time.
moon_sign.Cancer: Moon in Cancer is in its own sign, giving a deeply caring, intuitive and protective emotional nature. Memory, family bonds, mother and home are central, and the native feels others' moods readily. Nourishment comes from a safe home, shared meals, tradition, water and close affection. Sensitivity may bring moodiness, clinging or retreat into a shell when hurt. This placement tends to support a strong, receptive mind and good care for dependents. Emotional boundaries, regular rest and creative outlets keep feelings from overwhelming.
moon_sign.Leo: Moon in Leo gives a warm, proud and generous heart that wants recognition and loyalty. The mind is dignified, creative and inclined toward leadership, and the native feels nourished by appreciation, play, performance and being useful to others. Hurt pride or neglect can cause drama, sulking or a need for constant reassurance. The Sun as sign lord links emotional health to confidence and vitality. Spending time in sunlight, creative expression, and giving without expecting applause bring contentment. Humility and trust in quiet affection deepen the bond with loved ones.
moon_sign.Virgo: Moon in Virgo gives a careful, analytical and service-minded emotional nature. The mind notices details, seeks order and often worries about doing things well. Comfort comes from usefulness, clean and organised surroundings, healthy habits and solving practical problems. Self-criticism and anxiety can affect digestion and sleep. Mercury as sign lord gives a clear, adaptable mind and modest style. Nourishment comes from routines, meaningful work, nature and kind acceptance of imperfection. Learning to relax standards and receive care allows a gentle, reliable heart to show.
moon_sign.Libra: Moon in Libra gives a gentle, sociable mind that seeks harmony, fairness and companionship. Emotional comfort arises through relationships, beauty, art, music and balanced environments. The native dislikes conflict and may struggle to decide or to say no. Venus as sign lord brings charm, aesthetic taste and affection. Peace comes from partnership, a pleasant home, cooperative work and time to weigh choices. Self-reliance and clear expression of own needs prevent dependence on approval and keep the calm center steady.
moon_sign.Scorpio: Moon in Scorpio is debilitated in the classical view, yet it gives deep, intense and resilient feelings. Emotions run strong and private, with sharp intuition about hidden motives. The native may nurse hurts, test loyalty or swing between control and surrender. Nourishment comes from honest intimacy, privacy, research, healing work and meaningful rituals. Mars as sign lord adds courage and passion. Strong support from benefic aspects or a well-placed Moon softens the pattern. Forgiveness, physical release and trusted confidants transform emotional intensity into insight and strength.
moon_sign.Sagittarius: Moon in Sagittarius gives an optimistic, freedom-loving and philosophical mind. The native seeks meaning, learning, travel and honest company, and feels nourished by faith, teachers, open spaces and humor. Generosity and trust are natural, though restlessness and bluntness can hurt. Jupiter as sign lord brings hope and resilience in hardship. Peace comes through purposeful study, outdoor activity and a belief that gives direction. Staying attentive to details and others' feelings keeps ideals from becoming careless promises.
moon_sign.Capricorn: Moon in Capricorn gives a reserved, practical and self-controlled emotional nature. Feelings are held in check, and security is sought through achievement, structure and responsibility. The native may seem cool outwardly but is deeply dutiful and loyal. Saturn as sign lord can bring early seriousness and worry about the future. Nourishment comes from steady progress, respect, clear roles and quiet time. Allowing tenderness, humor and rest, and sharing burdens with trusted people, prevents emotional dryness and lets the mind grow warmer with age.
moon_sign.Aquarius: Moon in Aquarius gives a detached, thoughtful and friendly mind that values freedom and ideas. The native feels at ease in groups with shared causes, yet needs solitude to recharge. Emotions may be analysed rather than expressed, which can seem aloof to loved ones. Saturn as sign lord brings steadiness and long-term thinking. Nourishment comes from friendships, learning, humanitarian purpose and unconventional pursuits. Opening up about personal feelings and valuing small daily affections deepen closeness without losing independence.
moon_sign.Pisces: Moon in Pisces gives a compassionate, imaginative and deeply receptive mind that absorbs the moods around it. The native is drawn to music, poetry, devotion and quiet places, and often has strong intuition and dreams. Boundaries may blur, leading to escapism, oversensitivity or confusion. Jupiter as sign lord brings faith and kindness that help recovery from hardship. Nourishment comes from solitude, water, spiritual practice, creative work and gentle company. Consistent routines and discernment in whom to trust protect this tender nature.

Ashwini.text: Ashwini, the first nakshatra, spans the start of Aries and is ruled by Ketu in the Vimshottari system. It carries the energy of swiftness, healing and fresh beginnings. Natives are active, enthusiastic, pioneering and quick to help others, often with an interest in medicine, speed, sport or transport. Career leanings include healing professions, emergency work, engineering, riding, pioneering ventures and anything requiring prompt action. They learn fast and dislike waiting. Cautions include impulsiveness, impatience, starting without finishing and a tendency to push the body too hard. Grounding the energy with planning and rest allows the healing gift to mature.

Bharani.symbol: Yoni, the female organ of birth
Bharani.text: Bharani lies in Aries and is ruled by Venus. Presided over by Yama, lord of dharma and restraint, it deals with bearing responsibility, endurance and the cycle of creation and release. Natives are strong-willed, passionate, truthful and able to carry heavy burdens. They often have a sense of justice and intense feelings about pleasure and duty. Career leanings include law, finance, the arts, childbirth and care professions, and work with endings such as insurance or transitions. Cautions include extremes of indulgence and austerity, jealousy and self-imposed pressure. Moderation and clear values bring fulfillment.

Krittika.text: Krittika straddles Aries and Taurus and is ruled by the Sun. Its deity Agni, the sacred fire, gives a purifying, sharp and discerning quality. Natives are bright, direct, ambitious and critical of falsehood, often with strong appetites and protective instincts. Career leanings include leadership, military or administration, cooking, metalwork, editing, teaching and any field that cuts to the essential. Cautions include a cutting tongue, anger, pride and burning out through perfectionism. Warmth in speech and generosity soften the blade, turning criticism into constructive clarity and honor.

Rohini.text: Rohini lies in Taurus and is ruled by the Moon, which is exalted here. Associated with growth and creation, it gives beauty, charm, fertility and love of material pleasure. Natives are attractive, artistic, sensual and gifted in speech, with a strong desire for security and family. Career leanings include arts, fashion, agriculture, hospitality, finance, cosmetics and trade in goods. Cautions include possessiveness, vanity, attachment to comfort, and fixed opinions. Using charm and creative power for service rather than craving keeps its abundant fertility wholesome and lasting.

Mrigashira.text: Mrigashira spans Taurus and Gemini and is ruled by Mars. Its symbol, the searching deer, reflects curiosity and a gentle, restless seeking. Natives are inquisitive, charming, sensitive and fond of travel, learning and exploring ideas, places and people. Career leanings include research, writing, teaching, design, music, travel work and trade. They are good listeners yet may flit between interests. Cautions include indecision, nervousness, wandering attention and being easily distracted by novelty. Commitment to a chosen path and quiet time with nature turn constant seeking into real discovery.

Ardra.text: Ardra lies in Gemini and is ruled by Rahu. Presided over by Rudra, the storm god, it signifies upheaval that clears the way for renewal. Natives are intellectual, determined, emotionally intense and often face turning points that deepen understanding. Career leanings include research, technology, medicine, investigation, writing, and crisis management or reform. Cautions include harsh speech, moodiness, ingratitude and a tendency to dwell on loss. Compassion, gratitude and ethical use of a sharp mind transform storms into insight and make the native a source of fresh solutions.

Punarvasu.text: Punarvasu spans Gemini and Cancer and is ruled by Jupiter. Its deity Aditi, mother of the gods, signifies return, renewal and boundless abundance. Natives are optimistic, kind, adaptable and able to recover well after setbacks, with a love of home, learning and philosophy. Career leanings include teaching, counseling, writing, publishing, hospitality, spiritual work and travel. They often return to places or ideas after journeys. Cautions include scattered effort, over-trust, and dependence on comfort. Steady purpose and generosity help them make use of the protective grace this star offers.

Pushya.text: Pushya lies in Cancer and is ruled by Saturn. Considered the most auspicious of the nakshatras, its deity Brihaspati bestows nourishment, wisdom and guidance. Natives are responsible, caring, dutiful and respected for reliability and moral sense. Career leanings include teaching, counseling, law, government, agriculture, charity, medicine and work in service of communities. Cautions include rigidity, over-seriousness, worry and carrying others' burdens until exhausted. Balance of duty with rest and warmth lets this nurturing and steady star build lasting security for family and society.

Ashlesha.text: Ashlesha lies in Cancer and is ruled by Mercury. Its serpent deities bring penetrating insight, magnetism and an interest in the hidden. Natives are perceptive, strategic, resourceful and psychologically astute, often with a strong survival instinct. Career leanings include psychology, medicine, pharmacy, research, politics, occult studies and negotiation. Cautions include secretiveness, suspicion, manipulation and emotional clinging. Honesty and trust-building direct the cunning intelligence toward healing and protection, and the transformative power of kundalini-like energy becomes a gift to others.

Magha.text: Magha lies in Leo and is ruled by Ketu. Connected with the ancestors, it brings dignity, tradition and a regal bearing. Natives respect lineage, seek status and recognition, and often hold authority or inherit duties and property. Career leanings include government, administration, heritage work, history, politics, management and ceremonial roles. They are generous hosts yet expect respect. Cautions include pride, arrogance, resentment of slights and clinging to the past. Humility and gratitude to elders and honest service make their leadership genuinely noble.

Purva Phalguni.symbol: Front legs of a bed or hammock
Purva Phalguni.text: Purva Phalguni lies in Leo and is ruled by Venus. Its deity Bhaga governs enjoyment, fortune and marital happiness. Natives are warm, creative, sociable, romantic and fond of leisure, art and festivity. Career leanings include entertainment, the arts, hospitality, luxury goods, counseling, relationships and event management. They have magnetic charm and generosity. Cautions include indulgence, laziness, vanity and difficulties through excess pleasure-seeking. Disciplined creativity and responsible commitment allow the fortune of this star to last and be shared with others.

Uttara Phalguni.text: Uttara Phalguni spans Leo and Virgo and is ruled by the Sun. Its deity Aryaman presides over contracts, friendship and patronage. Natives are reliable, kind, helpful and gifted at building lasting alliances and supporting others. Career leanings include administration, social service, teaching, management, law, diplomacy and partnership-based businesses. They value honor and fairness. Cautions include overextending in favors, being taken for granted, and rigidity about duty. Healthy boundaries and mutual respect let their dependable generosity bring stable prosperity and loyal friends.

Hasta.text: Hasta lies in Virgo and is ruled by the Moon. Its deity Savitar, the inspiring sun, favors skill, craftsmanship and the capacity to manifest ideas. Natives are clever, witty, resourceful and good with their hands and with speech. Career leanings include crafts, healing, writing, trade, design, technology, comedy and handiwork of all kinds. Cautions include restlessness, anxiety, cunning used for petty ends, and nervous tension. Using dexterity with integrity and calming the mind through routine channel their quick intelligence into dependable accomplishment.

Chitra.text: Chitra spans Virgo and Libra and is ruled by Mars. Its deity Tvashtar, the divine architect, gives artistry, design sense and striking presence. Natives are creative, magnetic, stylish and ambitious, often with a love of beauty and craftsmanship. Career leanings include architecture, engineering, fashion, jewelry, art, design, film and technical work. Cautions include vanity, restlessness, self-focus and unease with ordinary routine. Channeling energy into meaningful construction and honest self-presentation lets the brilliance of this star build works that last.

Swati.symbol: Young sprout swaying in the wind or coral
Swati.text: Swati lies in Libra and is ruled by Rahu. Its deity Vayu, the wind god, grants independence, flexibility and a love of movement. Natives are adaptable, diplomatic, enterprising and self-reliant, with a talent for trade and negotiation. Career leanings include business, law, travel, aviation, diplomacy, sales and independent professions. They bend rather than break under pressure. Cautions include indecision, scattered effort, a wish to avoid commitment and sensitivity to criticism. Rooting oneself in values and staying consistent helps this free spirit grow steadily.

Vishakha.text: Vishakha spans Libra and Scorpio and is ruled by Jupiter. Its deities Indra and Agni represent aim, ambition and tenacity. Natives are determined, goal-focused, persuasive and ready to work long toward a target. Career leanings include politics, management, leadership, law, sales, military, teaching and organizing campaigns. They are strong in debate and persistence. Cautions include jealousy, impatience, single-minded striving, and anger when blocked. Cooperation and appreciation of the process, not just the prize, bring satisfying success.

Anuradha.text: Anuradha lies in Scorpio and is ruled by Saturn. Its deity Mitra, god of friendship, gives devotion, loyalty and the ability to cooperate in groups. Natives are friendly, disciplined, organized and successful through relationships, often finding fortune or meaning far from their birthplace. Career leanings include organizations, trade, counseling, diplomacy, travel work, research and spiritual service. Cautions include moodiness, hidden resentment, overwork and difficulty letting go. Open communication and trust deepen their gift for lasting friendships and shared achievement.

Jyeshtha.text: Jyeshtha lies in Scorpio and is ruled by Mercury. Its deity Indra, chief of the gods, grants seniority, protective instinct and a strong sense of authority. Natives are capable, responsible, courageous and often take on leadership or elder roles early. Career leanings include administration, military, police, management, politics, investigation and protective professions. Cautions include pride, secrecy, rivalry, a sense of being unappreciated and tension with peers. Humility, generosity and sharing credit turn natural command into trusted guardianship.

Mula.text: Mula lies in Sagittarius and is ruled by Ketu. Its deity Nirriti, goddess of dissolution, drives investigation to the root of matters. Natives are probing, truth-seeking, determined and frequently experience upheavals that remove false foundations. Career leanings include research, philosophy, medicine (especially herbal), investigation, spirituality and fields that deal with fundamentals. Cautions include disruptive changes, blunt criticism, restlessness and troubles with early support. Accepting change and building a real foundation of truth transform loss into strong, authentic purpose.

Purva Ashadha.text: Purva Ashadha lies in Sagittarius and is ruled by Venus. Its deity Apas, the waters, grants purification, invigoration and persuasive enthusiasm. Natives are proud, confident, friendly and optimistic, with a love of debate and a refreshing influence on others. Career leanings include teaching, law, public speaking, shipping, water-related industries, motivational work and the arts. Cautions include stubbornness, overconfidence and argumentative moods. Listening and consistent effort balance their natural invincibility and make their persuasion genuinely uplifting.

Uttara Ashadha.symbol: Elephant tusk or planks of a bed
Uttara Ashadha.text: Uttara Ashadha spans Sagittarius and Capricorn and is ruled by the Sun. Its deities, the Vishvedevas, signify universal principles and final victory. Natives are principled, steady, ambitious and often succeed late but firmly through perseverance. Career leanings include administration, government, law, military, public service, engineering and leadership of lasting institutions. Cautions include seriousness, delays in recognition, rigid standards and isolation from burden. Patience, ethics and warmth win enduring respect and a legacy that outlasts effort.

Shravana.text: Shravana lies in Capricorn and is ruled by the Moon. Its deity Vishnu, preserver, makes listening, learning and connection its chief themes. Natives are attentive, knowledgeable, reputable and good at gathering and passing on information. Career leanings include teaching, counseling, media, communications, music, administration and traditional or spiritual study. Cautions include gossip, over-reliance on others' opinions and worry about reputation. Mindful listening and sharing wisdom responsibly lend them respected standing and steady fortune.

Dhanishta.text: Dhanishta spans Capricorn and Aquarius and is ruled by Mars. Its deities, the eight Vasus, are linked to wealth and abundance. Natives are energetic, ambitious, rhythmic, generous and good at earning and organizing. Career leanings include music, sports, real estate, engineering, military, entrepreneurship and group leadership. Cautions include impatience, a combative streak, restlessness in relationships and overspending. Cooperation, patience and gratitude convert dynamism into stable prosperity and harmonious teamwork.

Shatabhisha.text: Shatabhisha lies in Aquarius and is ruled by Rahu. Its deity Varuna, lord of cosmic waters, links it to healing, secrecy and a hundred remedies. Natives are independent, private, research-minded and often drawn to science, alternative medicine and mystical study. Career leanings include medicine, pharmacy, astrology, engineering, technology, investigation and solitary specialist work. Cautions include isolation, secretiveness, melancholy and stubborn views. Opening up to trusted people and applying knowledge to healing makes their depth valued and fulfilling.

Purva Bhadrapada.symbol: Front of a funeral cot or sword
Purva Bhadrapada.text: Purva Bhadrapada spans Aquarius and Pisces and is ruled by Jupiter. Its deity Aja Ekapada, the one-footed goat or fiery sun, blends intensity and spiritual aspiration. Natives are passionate, idealistic, unconventional and capable of both warmth and austerity. Career leanings include teaching, research, occult sciences, reform work, medicine, finance and fields requiring conviction. Cautions include extremes of mood, anxiety, secretiveness and sharp speech. Disciplined spiritual practice and balance between ideals and daily life let their transformative energy serve others.

Uttara Bhadrapada.symbol: Back of a funeral cot or twins
Uttara Bhadrapada.text: Uttara Bhadrapada lies in Pisces and is ruled by Saturn. Its deity Ahir Budhnya, the serpent of the deep, gives stability, depth and endurance. Natives are calm, wise, compassionate and capable of great patience, often with an interest in spirituality and service. Career leanings include counseling, charity, healing, research, teaching, finance and quiet leadership. Cautions include laziness, over-withholding emotions, and delays. Engaging actively in worthwhile causes channels their reserves of strength and gentleness into lasting benefit.

Revati.text: Revati, the last nakshatra, ends Pisces and is ruled by Mercury. Its deity Pushan protects travelers and herds, bringing nourishment and safe passage. Natives are gentle, kind, imaginative, protective and trusted by others, often with artistic or spiritual leanings. Career leanings include care professions, animal work, travel, arts, teaching, hospitality and charitable service. Cautions include naivety, indecision, vulnerability to exploitation and dreaminess. Practical discernment and clear boundaries allow their compassion and guidance to benefit many, closing the cycle with grace.

Sun.1: Sun in the first house gives a dignified bearing, strong will, leadership and a lean, bright-eyed look. Vitality is good, though pride, heat and impatience can arise. In Aries (exalted) or Leo it shines; in Libra it asks for humility. Self-reliance grows, and its dasha often raises status, with a need to manage ego and eyes or head complaints. In Aries or Leo the glow is healthy and commanding; in Libra the same placement turns self-doubting until later years.
Sun.2: Sun in the second house supports authority in speech, family standing and earnings linked to government, gold or leadership. Speech can be forceful or proud, and family bonds may involve friction with ego. Wealth comes through effort and position rather than inheritance. Cautions include harsh words, eyesight or dental sensitivity, and spending on status. Family elders, especially the father's side, may set the tone, and the right eye and teeth are sensitive points.
Sun.3: Sun in the third house gives courage, initiative and strong will to excel in skills, writing, media or competition. Younger siblings may be helped or may rival the native. It is a favorable placement for self-made progress, short travels and perseverance. Cautions include stubbornness with relatives and overconfidence. Its dasha rewards bold, steady effort. Aspects from Mars or Saturn steady the courage; younger brothers often take a clear role during the Sun dasha.
Sun.4: Sun in the fourth house is classically a mixed placement. It can bring property, a prominent home and public standing later in life, yet may reduce domestic peace or distance the native from the mother or birthplace. Emotional contentment improves by inner work. Aries Sun is strong here; vehicles, land and education need conscious care. The heart, chest and the father's relationship with the home are involved, and Jupiter's glance brings real comfort.
Sun.5: Sun in the fifth house favors intelligence, creativity, leadership and a strong connection with children and teachers. Speculation and politics may rise but need prudence. Children may be few or strong-willed, and relations with them need respect. Sun in its own or friendly signs gives authority and good judgment; afflicted, it creates pride or stomach strain. The first child or the pupil-teacher bond is highlighted, and stomach acidity responds to calmer eating.
Sun.6: Sun in the sixth house is traditionally strong for overcoming enemies, debts and illness. It gives stamina, competitive skill and success in service, government or medicine. Maternal relatives may be a source of friction. Cautions include digestive heat and workplace power struggles. The dasha rewards discipline and fair dealings with a growth in standing. The dasha is usually a period of promotion or legal wins, with uncle-type relatives and the digestive fire in focus.
Sun.7: Sun in the seventh house brings a partner of dignity or strong character, and a wish for leadership in partnership. Marriage may be delayed or tested by ego clashes, so equality and respect matter. Business through partnership can succeed. In Libra it is debilitated and demands humility; benefic aspects ease relationships and public dealings. A father-in-law or a partner from an official family may feature, and Venus aspects ease the pride.
Sun.8: Sun in the eighth house can give interest in research, occult study, inheritance and long life with periods of transformation. Vitality may fluctuate, and relationships with authority or the father may involve loss and lessons. Eyes and heart need attention. Spiritual depth and investigation grow through crises; the dasha asks for patience and humility. Father's health or inheritance matters surface in the dasha, and the eyes and heart deserve checkups.
Sun.9: Sun in the ninth house is a classical strength: it supports dharma, higher learning, fortune from authority and a respectful relationship to father and teachers. The native tends to be principled, philosophical and sometimes dogmatic. Pilgrimages, foreign contacts and mentorship are favored. Afflictions may cause friction with elders or rigid belief. Jupiter's aspect crowns this with respected gurus; Saturn's can make the father's guidance severe or distant.
Sun.10: Sun in the tenth house is highly regarded for career, power and public recognition. It gives ambition, authority and success in administration, politics or leadership roles. Directional strength here helps reputation grow with age. Cautions include workaholism, ego battles with superiors and neglect of private life. The dasha often marks professional peaks. Exalted in Aries it gives rank by merit, and the Sun dasha often opens the doors of government or senior management.
Sun.11: Sun in the eleventh house gives gains, influential friends, and fulfillment of ambitions, especially through government, organizations and elder siblings. Income grows steadily with persistence and networks. It is considered a very good placement. Cautions include expecting too much from groups or attracting admirers for status alone. Gains often come from eldest siblings or influential groups, and the dasha commonly lifts income in one clear step.
Sun.12: Sun in the twelfth house tends to reduce outward ego and turns the mind inward, toward foreign lands, spirituality, solitude or hospitals. Expenses, sleep disturbance and eye strain are cautions, and recognition may be delayed. It supports service behind the scenes, retreat and detachment. With support, it deepens humility and insight. Eyes, sleep and the left side of the body are sensitive, and the dasha may involve postings abroad or a hospital setting.

Moon.1: Moon in the first house gives a sensitive, adaptable nature, a rounded or attractive face and strong public appeal. Moods fluctuate with the lunar phase, and the body responds to emotion. A waxing Moon brings confidence and popularity; a waning one calls for care of mind. Travel and change are common, and the dasha stresses self-image. A full Moon brings radiance and popularity, while a dim Moon near the Sun asks for steady sleep and lighter company.
Moon.2: Moon in the second house favors a pleasant voice, family attachment, love of food and fluctuating but generally accumulating wealth. Income may relate to the public, food, liquids or women. Moods can influence spending. Strong when waxing, it supports nourishing speech; afflicted, it causes worry over security and inconsistency in finances. Mother and maternal relatives influence the family wealth, and the face, throat and eating patterns reflect moods.
Moon.3: Moon in the third house gives imagination, communication skills, curiosity and close ties with siblings and neighbors. It supports writing, media, short trips and creative hobbies. Courage is more emotional than aggressive, and the mind may be restless. Its dasha supports learning and networking, with attention needed to anxiety or scattered effort. Younger sisters or female neighbors are close, and Mercury's aspect sharpens writing and speech during the Moon dasha.
Moon.4: Moon in the fourth house is naturally strong, giving emotional contentment, a close bond with the mother, attachment to home, property and vehicles. Inner peace and good education are favored. The native benefits from a quiet home and roots. Afflictions bring unsettled domestic life or over-sensitivity. The dasha tends to be comfortable and nurturing. This is directional strength for the Moon, so the heart-mind and chest are well protected; Saturn's aspect cools warmth.
Moon.5: Moon in the fifth house gives a creative, emotional and affectionate mind, interest in poetry, art, teaching and children. Intuition is good, and romance is important. Waxing Moon supports happiness through children and study; afflicted, it causes mood-based decisions or worry about offspring. Speculation should be careful. Moon in Cancer, Taurus or Pisces here lifts imagination, and the dasha often arrives with a child or a creative flowering.
Moon.6: Moon in the sixth house can bring emotional sensitivity to daily stress, digestive or sleep issues, and concern about service and health. It also gives caring skills for nursing, food and helping professions. Waning Moon requires discipline with worry; waxing Moon helps in work. Conflicts with maternal relatives and over-worry should be managed. The mother's side or women colleagues may bring friction, and the stomach and lymph system are the body parts to watch.
Moon.7: Moon in the seventh house gives a gentle, attractive and caring partner, popularity and gain through public dealings. Emotional dependence on a spouse is strong and moods influence relationships. A waxing Moon supports harmony and good business; a weak one may bring fluctuations. Dasha supports marriage, travel and partnership. Venus or Jupiter aspecting steadies the marriage, whereas Saturn's aspect brings emotional distance; the dasha often brings a wedding.
Moon.8: Moon in the eighth house gives deep intuition, interest in the occult, research and changeable fortunes. Emotional intensity and anxiety may show, and the mother may face health issues. Longevity is usually supported, with transformations along the way. Waxing Moon softens the placement. It calls for emotional healing and psychological honesty. The mother's health or fluid-related ailments can feature, and Jupiter's aspect turns anxiety into psychological insight.
Moon.9: Moon in the ninth house is favorable for fortune, devotion, higher learning and travel, especially to sacred or distant places. The mind is optimistic, ethical and receptive to teachers. A close bond with the mother and father may exist. The dasha often brings good luck and spiritual growth, with some changeable beliefs. Maternal grandparents and spiritual teachers support fortune, and the dasha often carries a pilgrimage or an overseas move.
Moon.10: Moon in the tenth house gives popularity, public work and a career with changing phases, often involving people, care, food, trade or hospitality. Reputation fluctuates with moods but is generally supported. A waxing Moon is stronger. The native seeks emotional meaning in work, and the dasha gives recognition with variety. Directional strength is not formal here, but the dasha often brings visibility; work with the public, nursing or liquids suits well.
Moon.11: Moon in the eleventh house gives gains through many friends, women and public networks, with steady fulfillment of wishes. It supports social ease and sensitivity. Income may fluctuate but tends to rise. Afflictions cause dependence on others' opinions. Waxing Moon is especially fruitful and the dasha fulfills hopes. Women friends and the elder sister are helpful; the dasha usually realizes a long-held wish tied to the public.
Moon.12: Moon in the twelfth house brings a dreamy, private and compassionate mind, interest in solitude, foreign lands and spirituality. Sleep may be vivid or disturbed, and expenses are fluid. Emotional retreat can be healing if balanced. It supports charity, imagination and detachment; worry and isolation need care. Sleep, the left eye and fluid balance are sensitive, and the dasha frequently involves a stay in another city or country.

Mars.1: Mars in the first house gives vigor, courage, a muscular body and leadership, with scars or marks on the head. It makes one bold, competitive and quick-tempered. In Aries, Scorpio or Capricorn it is strong and can create the Ruchaka yoga. Caution is needed with accidents, anger and marital harmony (Manglik effect). Exalted in Capricorn it gives disciplined athletic strength; a Jupiter aspect cools the temper, Saturn's makes it simmer.
Mars.2: Mars in the second house can give forceful speech, family tensions, and wealth earned through effort, engineering, land or competition. Eating habits may be heated, and sarcasm may hurt. When well placed, speech has courage and accumulation is steady; afflicted, it causes disputes over money and Manglik effects. Calm speech helps greatly. The mouth, face and teeth are involved, and the Mars dasha can stir family arguments over land or inheritance.
Mars.3: Mars in the third house is a classical strength: courage, stamina, initiative and success in sports, military, technical work and self-made ventures. Relationships with siblings may involve rivalry or support. It gives a determined mind and a capacity to overcome obstacles. Excess aggression or recklessness should be restrained. Younger brothers are protective or competitive, and the arms, shoulders and ears are the sensitive points.
Mars.4: Mars in the fourth house tends to disturb domestic peace, though it can give land, property and vehicles. Tension with the mother or at home is possible, and one may live in places with change. Manglik effect applies. When strong, it supports real-estate and engineering. Inner calm, patience and a quiet home life help. In Capricorn it is exalted and builds property with force; the chest, mother's heat-related health and vehicles need attention.
Mars.5: Mars in the fifth house gives a bold, competitive intellect, sports ability and strategic mind. Children may be strong-willed, and their timing or number can be affected. Romance is passionate, and speculation risky. It supports teaching in technical fields. Anger in creative expression and stomach heat need attention. The first child may be energetic, and Mars in its own sign brings sporting or engineering brilliance in the dasha.
Mars.6: Mars in the sixth house is classically good, giving strength to defeat enemies, resolve debts and recover from illness. It supports competitive jobs, military, police, surgery and legal conflicts. Courage is high and stamina strong. Cautions include injuries, inflammation and unnecessary conflicts. The dasha rewards focused effort. The Mars dasha often brings courtroom or workplace wins, with injuries, boils and the lower abdomen needing attention.
Mars.7: Mars in the seventh house indicates a passionate, energetic partner and a strong Manglik effect. Marriage needs patience, mutual respect and care in temper. Business partnerships can be active but argumentative. In its own or friendly signs the placement is more stable; benefic support softens it. Delays or conflicts can be eased by maturity. The spouse often has a firm will; Jupiter's aspect softens this, and the husband in a woman's chart is the focus.
Mars.8: Mars in the eighth house gives intensity, research ability and interest in surgery, occult and hidden matters. Risks include accidents, surgeries, and sudden events, but it can also give longevity and inheritance. Manglik effects apply. Caution with vehicles, fire and tempers. The dasha brings transformations that strengthen resilience. Wounds, piles and the reproductive area are sensitive, and the dasha may involve surgery or a legacy through the spouse.
Mars.9: Mars in the ninth house gives a courageous, action-oriented approach to dharma, and defense of beliefs. Relations with father or teachers may be energetic or contentious. It supports fortune through effort, property and pioneering travels. Zeal in religion can become dogmatic. Directing energy into worthwhile causes brings good outcomes. Father or teacher may be a soldierly figure, and the thighs and hips suffer if zeal turns into reckless travel.
Mars.10: Mars in the tenth house is strongly positioned (directional strength), giving ambition, drive and success in leadership, engineering, military, sports, surgery or property fields. It supports courage in reputation and quick achievement. Cautions include temper at work, competitive conflicts and impulsiveness. Dasha often marks career gains. Strong in Capricorn, it gives drive for engineering, defence or surgery; the dasha frequently marks a rise to command.
Mars.11: Mars in the eleventh house gives steady gains, ambitious friends, and income through property, technology or competitive fields. Elder siblings may be supportive or dominant. Desires are fulfilled by energetic effort. This is considered a very good placement for Mars, with some caution about aggressive friends or overspending on goals. Elder brothers or friends in technical fields help, and the dasha pays off ambitions in property or competitive sectors.
Mars.12: Mars in the twelfth house can bring high expenses, hidden energy, strong bedroom and sleep matters, and conflicts that remain unseen. It also supports foreign work, hospitals, military and spiritual discipline. Manglik effect exists. Directed into charity, exercise or isolation work, it gives strength; anger and secret rivalry need care. Eyes, feet and the left side suffer if rest is neglected, and the dasha may involve confinement, a hospital or distant postings.

Mercury.1: Mercury in the first house gives a youthful, witty, communicative personality with a slim body and quick mind. Learning, humor, trade and writing come easily. In Virgo it is exalted and strongly intellectual; afflicted, it causes nervousness and scattered thought. The dasha is excellent for education, business and skill-building. Combustion by a close Sun dulls the speech, whereas an Aries or Gemini ascendant gets exceptional mental agility.
Mercury.2: Mercury in the second house supports eloquent speech, business sense, accumulation through trade, writing or analysis, and a learned family. Speech is persuasive and witty. Wealth rises through skills and communication. Afflictions may lead to inconsistent savings or sharp talk. The dasha favors earning through intellect. Maternal uncles and cousins may play a role in the family, and the voice, tongue and throat reflect the nerves.
Mercury.3: Mercury in the third house gives strong writing, communication and craft skills, curiosity and closeness to siblings. It supports media, sales, teaching and short travel. The mind is inventive and enterprising. Excessive restlessness or gossip should be avoided. The dasha rewards courage in expression and networking. Siblings are often chatty or business-minded, and the hands, fingers and shoulders are active; Mercury's dasha favors publishing.
Mercury.4: Mercury in the fourth house supports education, a comfortable home, knowledge about property and a talkative family environment. It gives a studious mind, interest in books and a fine vehicle or home. Emotional restlessness may appear. Directional gains in education and peaceful learning make the dasha supportive. Gemini or Virgo here supports teaching and degrees; the mother is educated, and lungs respond to calm, steady breathing.
Mercury.5: Mercury in the fifth house gives a sharp, creative intellect, talent for teaching, writing, mathematics and strategy. Children are intelligent, and romance is playful. Speculation requires caution. It favors advisory and research roles. If afflicted, overthinking and nervous stress appear. The dasha supports study and creative output. Exalted in Virgo it brings sharp mathematics and advice; the dasha often coincides with exams or the birth of a clever child.
Mercury.6: Mercury in the sixth house gives analytical skill for service, health, accounts, law and competition. Success against rivals arises through intelligence rather than force. Digestive or nervous issues may need care. Debts can be managed by planning. The dasha supports detailed work, though anxiety and criticism should be watched. Maternal uncles and employees feature, and the intestines and skin are tender; the dasha favors accountancy and legal work.
Mercury.7: Mercury in the seventh house gives a youthful, intelligent partner, skill in negotiation and success in business partnerships. Communication is central to relationships. The native may marry a talkative, educated person. Afflictions bring indecision or mixed motives. The dasha supports trade, contracts and public dealings. The spouse is often younger or business-minded; Venus or Jupiter's aspect adds warmth, Saturn's makes dealings formal.
Mercury.8: Mercury in the eighth house gives research ability, interest in occult, finance and hidden knowledge, plus inheritance and sudden insights. Nervous strain and skin issues are possible. Speech may be secretive. Longevity is usually supported. The dasha encourages investigation, psychology and analytical depth, with care in contracts. Skin, nerves and the secret stores of knowledge feature, and the dasha can reveal insurance, tax or research opportunities.
Mercury.9: Mercury in the ninth house supports higher education, writing, philosophy and teaching. The mind is open and curious about religion and law. Fortune comes through learning, publishing and travel. Skepticism or over-intellectualizing belief is possible. The dasha supports mentors, long journeys and scholarly work. Teachers who are scholars influence the life, and Jupiter's aspect turns clever ideas into real wisdom and publication.
Mercury.10: Mercury in the tenth house gives success in careers involving communication, business, accounts, IT, writing, teaching and trade. The native is versatile and respected for intelligence. It supports multiple income sources. If afflicted, indecision or changing jobs appears. The dasha often promotes professional skills and recognition. Mercury is strong here for commerce; the dasha often changes jobs for a better role in accounting, IT or media.
Mercury.11: Mercury in the eleventh house gives gains through trade, networks, writing and intelligent friends. Income is varied and steady, and desires are fulfilled by smart effort. Friends are young, witty or educated. It is a good placement, though restlessness in goals should be handled. The dasha supports expansion of connections. Younger friends and maternal uncles are helpful, and the Mercury dasha tends to multiply small incomes into a steady flow.
Mercury.12: Mercury in the twelfth house gives a private, imaginative mind suited to research, foreign work, writing in solitude and spiritual study. Expenses on education or travel are common. Nervous worry and sleep issues may arise. In Pisces it is debilitated yet may give subtle intuition. The dasha favors retreat and behind-the-scenes work. Debilitated in Pisces, the mind overworks yet gains intuition; the nervous system and sleep need regular care in the dasha.

Jupiter.1: Jupiter in the first house gives a dignified, optimistic, wise personality, good health and respect from others. It protects the life and brings blessing, teaching ability and ethical nature. In Cancer, Sagittarius or Pisces it is especially strong. Weight, overconfidence or complacency may need care. The dasha is generally growth-oriented. Exalted in Cancer it is a shield for the whole chart; the liver, thighs and waistline are the body parts to watch.
Jupiter.2: Jupiter in the second house gives wealth, a pleasing voice, learned family and good values. Speech is wise and generous, and savings grow with time. It supports banking, teaching and food-related fields. Over-indulgence or promises beyond means should be avoided. The dasha tends to strengthen finances and family life. Elders in the family and the right-side jaw are linked, and Jupiter's dasha tends to raise savings step by step.
Jupiter.3: Jupiter in the third house gives a thoughtful, moral approach to communication, supportive siblings and moderate courage. It supports writing, teaching and advisory work, though effort can be less aggressive. Cautions include complacency and uneven initiative. Gradual progress and good counsel make the dasha positive. Siblings are scholarly or advisory, and Jupiter's glance on the ninth gives lucky teachers while the dasha supports publishing.
Jupiter.4: Jupiter in the fourth house is a blessing for domestic happiness, property, education and a close bond with the mother. Peace of mind and good vehicles are indicated. It supports teaching, real estate and a spiritual home. Over-comfort or indulgence may be a mild caution. The dasha tends to bring contentment. Jupiter in Cancer is exalted here and gives deep contentment; the mother is wise, and the chest and heart are well supported.
Jupiter.5: Jupiter in the fifth house is a classical strength for intelligence, children, creativity, mantra practice and good advice. The native is wise, generous and respected as a mentor. Children are often supportive. Excess optimism in speculation should be handled. The dasha favors education, family growth and spiritual progress. A Jupiter dasha often brings a child, a degree or a mantra initiation; Saturn's aspect delays but does not deny.
Jupiter.6: Jupiter in the sixth house helps overcome enemies, debts and health issues through wisdom and service, though it can reduce its own natural benefits. Care of diet, liver and weight is needed. Legal and healing work are favored. Generosity may be taken advantage of. The dasha supports service and gradual resolution of problems. In Sagittarius or Pisces it protects from enemies; the pancreas, blood sugar and relatives who are creditors need caution.
Jupiter.7: Jupiter in the seventh house gives a wise, kind and supportive partner, good fortune in marriage and success in partnerships and public dealings. The native is fair and respected. Expectations in marriage may be high. Benefic support makes this placement very fortunate. The dasha is often favorable for relationships and business. The spouse is learned or religious, and in a woman's chart this is the husband's karaka; the dasha often brings marriage.
Jupiter.8: Jupiter in the eighth house gives longevity, interest in philosophy, occult and research, and inheritance or sudden support. Progress can feel delayed but is protected. Faith may be tested and rebuilt through crises. It supports insurance, healing and transformative learning. The dasha deepens spiritual understanding. A long life with sudden support from in-laws; the dasha can reveal research gifts and a gradual healing of fears.
Jupiter.9: Jupiter in the ninth house is highly auspicious: it supports dharma, fortune, higher education, gurus and a good relationship with father. Faith, ethics and pilgrimage bring benefit. The native may teach or guide others. Dogmatism is the only caution. The dasha tends to be fortunate and meaningful. Father or a guru is a respected figure, and in the dasha, journeys, higher degrees and charitable works increase merit.
Jupiter.10: Jupiter in the tenth house gives respected position, ethical career, success in teaching, law, finance, advising or administration. Reputation is built on wisdom and fairness. Growth is steady and lasts. Overconfidence or avoiding hard decisions is a mild risk. The dasha brings professional recognition and responsibility. In Cancer it is exalted and gives respected office; the dasha tends to promote one into advisory or judicial roles.
Jupiter.11: Jupiter in the eleventh house gives abundant gains, wise and generous friends, fulfilled desires and supportive elder siblings. Income arises from multiple sources, often through teaching, finance or networks. It is highly favorable for prosperity. Over-optimism about goals needs check. The dasha expands wealth and social standing. Elder siblings and wealthy friends help, and the dasha typically fulfils pending desires and adds a steady second income.
Jupiter.12: Jupiter in the twelfth house gives spiritual inclination, charity, foreign settlement and comfortable expenses on good causes. Sleep and inner peace are supported, and moksha-oriented pursuits may appear. Material gains may be modest or leave the homeland. Overspending or escapism needs care. The dasha supports retreat and philanthropy. In Pisces it is strong and favors ashrams, retreats and charity; the feet and sleep are sensitive, and the dasha often takes one abroad.

Venus.1: Venus in the first house gives an attractive appearance, charm, artistic taste and a love of comfort. The native is sociable and pleasant, with success in relationships and the arts. In Pisces it is exalted. Overindulgence, vanity or laziness need care. The dasha emphasizes beauty, partnership and pleasure. In Pisces it is exalted and wins affection; in Virgo it is weak and may bring self-critical moods about the face and skin.
Venus.2: Venus in the second house supports a sweet voice, family harmony, wealth, jewelry, good food and artistic or luxury-related earnings. Values center on comfort and relationships. Spending on luxury can be high. The dasha usually improves finances, though attachments to taste should stay moderate. The face, eyes and sweet foods feature, and the women of the family help; the dasha frequently improves jewelry and savings.
Venus.3: Venus in the third house gives artistic communication, gentle courage, pleasant siblings and success in music, writing, design or media. The native is charming but may lack aggressive drive. Short journeys are enjoyable. Laziness or fickleness may arise. The dasha supports creative skills and social networking. Sisters or female neighbors support artistic projects, and the throat and voice benefit from music during the Venus dasha.
Venus.4: Venus in the fourth house is strongly favorable for a beautiful home, vehicles, comforts, mother and domestic happiness. Education is refined, and peace of mind is supported. It supports real estate, decor and hospitality. Over-attachment to luxury is a mild caution. The dasha brings stability and enjoyment. The mother is graceful, and the dasha brings a new home or car; Saturn's aspect delays the comforts, and Mars adds heat.
Venus.5: Venus in the fifth house gives romance, artistic creativity, charm and affection toward children. Love affairs and creative expression are emphasized. It supports entertainment, teaching and design. Speculation and flirtation need prudence. The dasha is often pleasant for love, children and creative success. A Venus dasha often brings romance or a daughter; in Taurus or Libra the creative output has refined beauty.
Venus.6: Venus in the sixth house can weaken enjoyment in relationships through disagreements, health or service duties. It gives skill in beauty, healing or service-related fields, and ability to handle conflicts diplomatically. Kidney, sugar or reproductive issues need care. The dasha asks for balance between work and pleasure. In Virgo it is debilitated and may cause quarrels with the spouse or partner; the kidneys and urinary system need care.
Venus.7: Venus in the seventh house is classically good: a loving, attractive partner, harmony in marriage and success in partnerships. The native values romance and fairness. In Libra or Taurus it is stronger. Over-dependence or multiple attachments should be avoided. The dasha tends to favor relationships and business. In Libra or Taurus it is strong and gives a faithful partner; Mars's aspect adds passion, Saturn's an older spouse.
Venus.8: Venus in the eighth house can give inheritance, sensual depth, interest in occult and transformations in relationships. Longevity is typically supported, but pleasure may come with periods of loss or secrecy. Reproductive health needs care. The dasha encourages emotional honesty and growth through intimacy. The spouse's family wealth or inheritance can feature, and the reproductive and urinary systems need regular checks.
Venus.9: Venus in the ninth house gives fortune through refined ethics, art, devotion and higher learning. Relations with teachers and father are pleasant. Long journeys and cultural exchanges are favored. Comfort-oriented belief should become thoughtful. The dasha brings good luck, spiritual refinement and sometimes a foreign link. A Venus dasha may bring a refined teacher and journeys to cultural places; an eloquent but gentle father is shown.
Venus.10: Venus in the tenth house supports careers in arts, design, fashion, entertainment, luxury, diplomacy and hospitality. The native is respected for grace and tact. Success may come through women or cooperative ventures. Comfort-seeking can reduce drive. The dasha usually brings reputation and pleasant professional growth. Fame in the arts, cinema or luxury trade is possible; the dasha is a prime time for establishing a brand.
Venus.11: Venus in the eleventh house gives gains through art, relationships, friends and luxury-related work. Desires tend to be fulfilled, and social life is joyful. Income is steady and multiple. It is a strong placement, though overspending on social life should be watched. The dasha expands income and connections. Women friends and elder sisters help gains, and the dasha brings new vehicles, jewelry and steady social income.
Venus.12: Venus in the twelfth house is traditionally good for private pleasures, comfort in bed, foreign living and charity. Expenses on luxury and relationships rise, yet it also supports deep devotion and artistic retreat. In Pisces it is exalted. Secret attachments need care. The dasha fosters peace and spiritual refinement. Sleep is pleasant, and the feet and eyes benefit from comfort; the dasha often favors life abroad or a retreat.

Saturn.1: Saturn in the first house gives a lean, serious, reserved nature, with discipline, endurance and late maturity. Early life can feel heavy, and health requires regular care. In Libra, Capricorn or Aquarius it is strong and can bring authority. The dasha rewards patience and responsibility, but loneliness and pessimism need attention. In Capricorn, Aquarius or Libra it gives dignity; the bones, teeth and joints need steady care, and the dasha tests then rewards.
Saturn.2: Saturn in the second house can bring austere or measured speech, a restricted early family life and slow but lasting wealth. Savings come through persistence and thrift. Dental and eye concerns may arise. Cautions include harshness in speech and delay in finances. The dasha builds security through discipline. Family wealth is built slowly, and an elder's burdens may be inherited; the teeth, right eye and speech feel strain in the dasha.
Saturn.3: Saturn in the third house gives perseverance, patient courage and success through steady effort, writing, technical work and long-term skills. Siblings may be few, distant or burdened. Initiative is slow but reliable. This is considered a good placement. The dasha rewards hard work with solid progress. Younger siblings are few or serious, and the knees and hands work hard; the Saturn dasha rewards craft and technical skills.
Saturn.4: Saturn in the fourth house can bring a modest or burdened domestic life, distance from the mother, and delays in property. Peace of mind comes through maturity and work. Late-life stability and old homes or land are possible. In its own sign it is better. The dasha asks for patience in emotional matters. The mother or old property needs support, and the chest and knees can feel stress; Saturn's dasha settles one into a lasting home.
Saturn.5: Saturn in the fifth house may delay children or creativity, bring a serious mind and cautious studies. The native can be a disciplined teacher or researcher. Children may need patience and support. Anxiety about romance or speculation may occur. The dasha gives depth and mature results with effort. Saturn in Aquarius or Libra gives mature studies, and Jupiter's aspect helps with children; the dasha tests creative confidence.
Saturn.6: Saturn in the sixth house is traditionally good: it gives the capacity to endure, overcome enemies, handle labor and defeat debts. It supports service, law, health and structured work. Chronic complaints need regular care. The dasha rewards perseverance and brings victory over long-term obstacles. In the dasha, rivals fall away and debts clear through steady effort; the bones, colon and servants or workers are in focus.
Saturn.7: Saturn in the seventh house often delays marriage or brings a mature, serious or older partner. Commitments are deep once formed, though emotional distance may need work. Business partnerships are cautious. In Libra it is exalted and supportive. The dasha builds lasting relationships through patience and loyalty. In Libra it is exalted and gives a loyal spouse; the dasha often brings a marriage or a serious business bond after thirty.
Saturn.8: Saturn in the eighth house is often supportive of longevity, research, occult study and perseverance through crises. Obstacles and delays in inheritance or shared resources are possible. Chronic health matters need attention. The dasha deepens maturity and detachment, giving strength after difficulty. The dasha may involve a chronic issue, a legacy delay or a long study of the occult; the lower legs and bowels are sensitive.
Saturn.9: Saturn in the ninth house can delay fortune and strain the relationship with father or teachers, yet it builds a sober, ethical and disciplined approach to belief. Higher education and travel may be slow but rewarding. Orthodoxy should be balanced with flexibility. The dasha brings gradual dharmic growth. The father may be strict or far away, and the dasha delays travel yet builds a code of ethics; the thighs and hips ache.
Saturn.10: Saturn in the tenth house is strong (directional strength), giving a disciplined, responsible and ambitious career. Success grows slowly and lasts, often in administration, industry, law or public work. Heavy responsibilities and rigid authority are possible. The dasha often marks major professional consolidation after effort. Exalted-like power in public duty in the right signs; the dasha, especially after thirty-six, often creates a lasting position.
Saturn.11: Saturn in the eleventh house is highly favorable, bringing gradual, lasting gains, mature friends and fulfillment of ambitions through persistence. Income grows with age. Elder siblings may be serious or distant. It supports long-term networks and organizations. The dasha rewards steady labor with prosperity. Elder siblings and older friends help; the legs, calves and circulation are the body areas, and the dasha is rich in gains.
Saturn.12: Saturn in the twelfth house encourages detachment, solitude, foreign living and a spiritual or service orientation. Expenses, sleep issues or isolation may need care. It supports work in hospitals, ashrams or abroad. Discipline in meditation brings benefit. The dasha can bring losses of illusions and growth in wisdom. The feet, sleep and the left eye are sensitive, and the dasha may relocate one abroad or into a quiet, disciplined life of service.

Rahu.1: Rahu in the first house gives a magnetic, unconventional personality, ambition and a strong desire to be seen. Identity can feel restless or confusing, and the body may be affected by stress. It supports innovation and foreign connections. Honesty and grounding help turn magnetism into success. The dasha brings sudden changes of self-image. Rahu takes on the results of its sign lord and conjunctions; the skin, nerves and head are sensitive, and the dasha is eventful.
Rahu.2: Rahu in the second house gives unusual speech, large wealth ambitions and diverse family or food habits. Earnings may come through foreign or unconventional channels. Speech can be persuasive or evasive. Instability in finances or family harmony is possible. Truthful speech and clear budgeting give the best results in its dasha. The family may have mixed cultures or varied diets, and the mouth and teeth are sensitive; the Rahu dasha raises and destabilizes accounts.
Rahu.3: Rahu in the third house is considered good: it gives daring, risk-taking and success in media, technology, communication and travel. The native is enterprising and self-promoting. Siblings may be distant or unusual. Over-aggression or impulse should be avoided. The dasha tends to enlarge courage and reach. Younger siblings may live far away, and the ears, hands and shoulders are linked; the Rahu dasha rewards bold online or media ventures.
Rahu.4: Rahu in the fourth house can cause restlessness at home, changes of residence and a sense of emotional dissatisfaction. It may give foreign homes, unusual education and vehicle interest. Mother's health or relationship needs care. Establishing routines and inner peace helps. The dasha shifts domestic life. The mother's health or a lost home can feature, and the chest and heart need calm; the dasha may bring a foreign residence.
Rahu.5: Rahu in the fifth house gives unconventional creativity, intense intellect and interest in speculation, mantras or technology. Children matters may involve delay or unusual circumstances. Romance can be intense or complicated. Ethical conduct and careful risks are advised. The dasha can bring novelty and learning. Rahu in Gemini or Virgo here is intellectually brilliant; the dasha may arrive with a child, a degree or a speculative gain or loss.
Rahu.6: Rahu in the sixth house is traditionally favorable for defeating enemies, overcoming debts and succeeding in competitive, service or foreign work. It gives cleverness and stamina. Hidden health issues or conflicts should be watched. The dasha supports victory over obstacles through strategic action. Jupiter's aspect supports health; the dasha clears debts, defeats rivals and can bring foreign employment, though allergies appear.
Rahu.7: Rahu in the seventh house tends to bring unconventional partners or relationships, foreign or different-background spouses, and intense attraction. Stability needs honest communication. Business partnerships can be innovative but risky. The dasha magnifies relationship themes and requires clarity and loyalty. The spouse may come from a different culture; Saturn's aspect steadies it, and the dasha reorganizes partnerships suddenly.
Rahu.8: Rahu in the eighth house gives fascination with occult, research, mysteries and sudden transformations. Unexpected gains or losses and health surprises are possible. It can support deep psychology and investigation. Secrecy and fear may arise. Spiritual practice and prudent finances help in its dasha. Sudden inheritance or insurance matters appear, and the reproductive system and poisons or infections need care in the dasha.
Rahu.9: Rahu in the ninth house can challenge conventional beliefs, bringing foreign teachers, travel and unorthodox philosophy. Relationship with father or gurus may be distant or unusual. Fortune comes through innovation but requires integrity. The dasha stimulates exploration, questioning and cross-cultural learning. The father or guru may be foreign or unorthodox, and the thighs and hips link; the dasha often takes one to distant lands.
Rahu.10: Rahu in the tenth house is well placed for ambition, politics, technology, media and foreign career. The native seeks status and may rise rapidly. Reputation can fluctuate with strategy. Ethical clarity is important. The dasha often brings prominent career opportunities and bold professional change. Rahu in Aries, Taurus or Gemini gives fast fame; the dasha tends to bring sudden promotions and a public-facing role.
Rahu.11: Rahu in the eleventh house is a classical strength for material gains, influential networks and fulfillment of desires. It supports technology, innovation and large social circles. Friends may be diverse, and ambitions high. Beware of opportunistic associates. The dasha is often prosperous and expansive. Elder siblings or influential friends bring gains, and the Rahu dasha sharply raises income, especially through online business.
Rahu.12: Rahu in the twelfth house gives interest in foreign lands, hidden dealings, vivid dreams and spiritual or unusual experiences. Expenses and sleep disturbances can occur. It supports work abroad, isolation, research and healing. Clear boundaries prevent escapism. The dasha encourages release and subtle awareness. The feet and sleep are sensitive, and Ketu in the sixth supports hidden foes; the dasha often means foreign settlement.

Ketu.1: Ketu in the first house gives a detached, introspective and sometimes mystical personality. Identity feels fluid, and the native may be indifferent to appearance or recognition. Health may be sensitive to stress. It supports spiritual insight and independence. Self-awareness and grounding bring strength. The dasha prompts inner search. Ketu behaves like its dispositor, and Mars or Jupiter connections matter; the head and nerves are sensitive, and the dasha is introspective.
Ketu.2: Ketu in the second house can bring plain or sharp speech, detachment from family and wealth, and uneven savings. It supports spiritual values, simple living and research. Throat or dental matters need care. Truthful speech and contentment help. The dasha asks for letting go of attachment to money and status. Family ties may be thin, and the mouth, teeth and speech are involved; the Ketu dasha may turn finances plain or simple.
Ketu.3: Ketu in the third house gives quiet courage, independence and a spiritual or technical aptitude. Siblings may be distant or the native may act without need for support. It is generally favorable for determination. Communication can be brief. The dasha supports mastery of skills and subtle accomplishment. Younger siblings are independent, and the ears, shoulders and hands link; the dasha supports technical or research skills.
Ketu.4: Ketu in the fourth house can bring detachment from home, restlessness in domestic life and a spiritual or reserved heart. Property or relationship with the mother may feel uncertain. It favors inner peace through practice. Education may be unconventional. The dasha encourages emotional healing and simplicity. The mother or the home may feel distant, and the chest is sensitive; the dasha often brings a spiritual, quiet home.
Ketu.5: Ketu in the fifth house gives intuitive, spiritual and non-conformist intellect. Interest in mantra, philosophy and research is strong. Children matters may need patience. Romance may feel detached. It supports meditative practice and past-life skills. The dasha encourages inner development more than external pleasure. A Ketu dasha may bring a spiritual teacher or an intuitive child; the stomach and past-life talents feature.
Ketu.6: Ketu in the sixth house is well regarded for overcoming enemies, disease and debts without much effort. It gives strong intuition for healing and service. Digestive or hidden issues may require care. The dasha supports victory over obstacles with quiet strategy and spiritual strength. Maternal relatives and servants are linked, and the dasha supports healing arts; the intestines and skin need tending.
Ketu.7: Ketu in the seventh house can bring detachment in relationships, a spiritual or unusual partner and lessons about attachment. Marriage requires communication and patience. Business partnerships may be unstable. The dasha encourages maturity and release of expectations while valuing sincerity in commitments. The spouse may be spiritual or reserved, and the dasha tests attachment; the lower back and reproductive area are sensitive.
Ketu.8: Ketu in the eighth house is often supportive of occult study, spiritual transformation and research. Sudden events may occur, but protection is also indicated. Health issues in digestive or hidden areas need watching. The dasha deepens intuition, detachment and inner healing. Inheritance may be lost or gained suddenly, and the dasha reveals occult talents; the genitals and rectum need care.
Ketu.9: Ketu in the ninth house gives a spiritual, unconventional or detached view of dharma, with interest in mysticism and past-life learning. Relationship with father or teachers may be distant. Fortune is inward rather than material. The dasha brings philosophical insight and pilgrimage tendencies. The father or teacher may be distant or very spiritual, and the dasha brings pilgrimages; the thighs and hips feel stress.
Ketu.10: Ketu in the tenth house can give a career of research, spiritual work, technical specialization or behind-the-scenes contributions. Recognition may come without seeking. Job changes or indifference to status are possible. The dasha emphasizes purposeful action and detachment from results. The career may serve behind the scenes, in research or healing; the dasha tends to detach from the need for applause.
Ketu.11: Ketu in the eleventh house is considered favorable, giving gains through subtle effort, a small circle of spiritual or loyal friends and fulfillment without much struggle. Ambition may be low-key. Occasional disappointments in groups are possible. The dasha brings quiet gains and wisdom about desire. Few but loyal friends appear, and elder siblings may be distant; the dasha fulfils desires almost quietly, with the calves involved.
Ketu.12: Ketu in the twelfth house is a classical placement for moksha, giving spiritual inclination, meditation, solitude and strong intuition. Expenses may be modest or charitable, and foreign or secluded living is possible. Sleep and escapism need care. The dasha supports liberation from attachments and deep inner peace. The feet and sleep link here; the dasha favors ashram life, retreat or foreign work and a deep sense of freedom.
